chunks: And from his sayings (peace be upon him): He had sent a man from his companions to learn the state of a group from the army of Kufa who had decided to join the Kharijites, and they were afraid of him (peace be upon him),
When the man returned to him, he said to him: 'Did they feel secure and stay, or did they feel weak and leave?' The man replied, 'They have left, O Commander of the Faithful.'
Then he (peace be upon him) said:
ai.seo_question: What was the reason for the Kufa army's hesitation before joining the Kharijites according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha highlights Imam Ali’s strategic assessment of the Kufa army's morale during the Battle of Siffin, where he discerned that their departure was driven by cowardice rather than a secure decision to remain. The companion’s concise reply underscores the Imam’s acute political insight into the psychological fragility of his troops amidst the internal strife with Muawiyah. This moment reflects the broader Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam’s knowledge of the unseen (Ilm al-Ghayb) and his ability to interpret subtle social dynamics.
